questions.q: What is a CSPM tool fundamentally doing, according to this lesson?
options: Running penetration tests against production workloads automatically
Continuously reading actual cloud configuration via APIs and comparing it against a library of known-good rules, flagging mismatches as findings
Replacing the need for identity providers like Entra ID or AWS IAM
Generating cost forecasts based on resource usage
questions.explain: CSPM tools continuously assess real configuration state against known rules (CIS Benchmarks, regulatory requirements, vendor best practices) and surface mismatches as findings.

questions.q: How is Microsoft Defender for Cloud's secure score calculated?
options: It is a single number set manually by an administrator
It is based only on the number of resources deployed, regardless of configuration
As a weighted aggregate of individual security controls, each scored as the ratio of healthy to total applicable resources, multiplied by the control's point weight
It is identical for every subscription regardless of which resources are deployed
questions.explain: The secure score aggregates security controls, each contributing points based on (healthy resources / total applicable resources) times that control's weight; controls with no applicable resources contribute zero points.

questions.q: How does AWS Security Hub's approach to scoring differ structurally from Defender for Cloud's single secure score?
options: Security Hub has no scoring mechanism at all
Security Hub only scores EC2 instances, nothing else
Security Hub ignores GuardDuty and Inspector findings entirely
Security Hub aggregates findings from enabled standards and integrated services, showing a pass/fail percentage per standard rather than one combined blended score
questions.explain: Security Hub normalizes findings from its own checks plus services like GuardDuty and Inspector, and shows compliance per enabled standard (e.g., CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark) rather than one single blended number.

questions.q: Per this lesson, what does a high secure score or a '100% passed' Security Hub standard NOT guarantee?
options: That an attacker is not already inside the environment, or that risks outside the checked rule set don't exist
That any configuration has ever been checked
That the cloud provider's infrastructure is physically secured
That the organization has an identity provider configured
questions.explain: CSPM measures known, checked configuration state — it does not detect active intrusions (that's threat detection's job) and says nothing about risks the rule set doesn't check for.

questions.q: Why does the lesson caution against simply fixing the highest-point-value recommendation first in every case?
options: Because point values are always randomly assigned and meaningless
Because high-point recommendations are never actionable
Because fixing recommendations has no effect on the secure score
Because a lower-scored recommendation affecting an actual internet-facing production workload can matter more than a higher-scored one on an isolated dev environment
questions.explain: Point value is a reasonable general prioritization heuristic, but it doesn't account for which specific resources matter most in a given environment — actual risk context should still guide prioritization.
